# moddotplot-rs v0.2.0

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This is the first public non-beta release of the browser-native moddotplot-rs 0.2
series. It combines compressed whole-genome uptake, interactive feature tracks, and
configurable heatmap rendering in a static application that keeps sequence and
annotation data inside the browser. It is released as a functional preview for public
evaluation, not as comprehensively research-validated software.

## Highlights

* Plain, gzip, and BGZF multi-FASTA input with ordered streaming, bounded parallel BGZF
  decompression, fast bulk base packing, sparse invalid-base storage, and a 3 GiB
  application admission budget.
* Stackable GC% and CpG observed/expected tracks with unsmoothed per-column bars,
  mouseover values, cached panning, and immediate stale-track blanking.
* Plain, gzip, and BGZF BED3–12, GFF3, and GTF feature tracks with sequence-aware axis
  assignment, UCSC colors, grouped gene models, one-to-ten-row packing, mouseovers,
  midpoint-based direct reordering, and drag-away disabling.
* Adjustable heatmap minimum, midpoint, and maximum mapping; multiple palettes; white
  and black plot backgrounds; exact terminal k-mer diagonals; and viewport-preserving
  parameter changes.
* Responsive desktop layout with compact axes and labels, centered plot assembly,
  control-panel status and memory reporting, and local FASTA/annotation validation
  dialogs.

## Whole-genome validation

The supplied HG002 v1.2 BGZF multi-FASTA contains 47 records and 5,999,430,218 bases.
In installed Google Chrome on the release host, every record was retained in 28.0
seconds, the initial self-dotplot reached Ready in 35.8 seconds, and reported
application memory was approximately 1.52 GiB. The supplied complete CHM13 and HG002
assemblies, compressed CHM13 gene annotation, and compressed centromeric satellite
annotation also passed maintainer testing with expected behavior and performance.

## Scientific regression

The release-mode estimator/HLL/fingerprint sweep and projection scheduling benchmark
pass. For the production 1,024-register, HLL p10 verified-winner configuration, mean
absolute ANI error was 0.008108 and P95 absolute ANI error was 0.025736 on the bounded
validation matrix. No tested fingerprint collision was observed. The preview and
detailed scientific configuration digests remain `58e084b7190f4d93` and
`bc5c5131ad1c9a20`, respectively.

## Verification

* Rust formatting, strict Clippy checks, 59 executed Rust tests, and wasm32 compilation
  pass.
* All 34 TypeScript unit tests pass.
* All 44 real-browser executions pass across Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, and installed
  Google Chrome.
* The production Wasm/UI build, documentation checks, SBOM generation, static privacy
  audit, and package inventory pass.
* Two clean builds produce byte-identical deployable static assets.

## Known limitations

* The release is a functional preview, not comprehensively research-validated software.
* Wasm32 has a 4 GiB linear address-space ceiling; the 3 GiB application admission
  budget reserves space for allocator, stack, transient, and plotting allocations.
* BigWig, BigBed, VCF, and indexed remote annotation sources are not supported.
* Imported annotations and loaded sequences are session-local and are discarded on
  reload.
* Approximate identity below roughly 80% remains outside the target operating regime.
* Numeric/high-resolution image export and stable numeric/pixel goldens remain open
  work.

No deployment, upload, or hosted URL is part of this release process.
